history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED. Sunhari Kothi ('Golden Mansion') is a secular heritage mansion and museum in Tonk city, near Bada Kua on Najar Bagh road - NOT a temple. Built in 1824 (per travel literature; patronage attribution to Nawab Ibrahim Ali Khan per project brief - FLAG: Wikipedia records Ibrahim Ali Khan succeeding as Nawab only in 1867, so the 1824 date or the patron attribution needs verification) as a residence with a famous 'Shishmahal' hall: walls polished with gold leaf, glass/mirror work, flower paintings, mother-of-pearl inlay and Pachhikari & Meenakari work. The Government of Rajasthan has gazetted it a historical place; renovation work has been ongoing. IGNCA ASI record RJ/TNK-001 ('Nawab ki Kothi', Tennis Court, Raj Talkies Road, Bada Kuan, Tonk) is a candidate match for this site (verify before merging).

town_description: Sunhari Kothi stands in Tonk city, the former capital of the Tonk princely state (1817-1947) - the only Muslim-ruled state in Rajputana, nicknamed 'Nawabi Nagari' and the 'Lucknow of Rajasthan'. Tonk blends Rajput and Mughal architecture and is famed for its havelis, mosques and the Arabic-Persian Research Institute.
